newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares oscillate in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares oscillate in early trade.

text.p: Singapore shares opened slightly higher on Wednesday as large industrial and blue chip shares regained some ground on a mild bout of bargain-hunting.
"The index is just oscillating," said one institutional dealer. "Today's gainers are basically yesterday's lowers."
By 0230 GMT the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 8.41 points at 2,070.39 on a moderate 18.8 million shares.

Top gainers included the foreign tranche of Singapore Press Holdings (SPH), due to report its annual results at the end of this week, and Singapore Air (SIA), which bounced back from recent heavy selling after disappointing half-year figures.
SPH foreign was up 50 cents at Singapore $24.30. SIA foreign was up 30 cents at S$12.80.
Dealers said foreign buying was still very low with most overseas funds waiting for the government to announce the next set of economic indicators before deciding whether to buy.

Singapore is expected to announce figures soon which analysts are forecasting to show its economy grew only two to three percent year-on-year in the third quarter, down from 10.9 percent in the first three months of the year.
The lower growth is due to a slowdown in demand for electronics products, on which Singapore is heavily dependent.
